source_metadata.exact_title: Hepatology: Emerging Paradigms in MASLD, Viral Hepatitis, Cholestatic Liver Disease, Portal Hypertension and Hepatocellular Carcinoma

atoms.canonical_statement: The review synthesizes principal scientific advances presented at the first Paris International Liver Meeting 2026 across steatotic liver disease, viral hepatitis, cholestatic liver disease, hepatocellular carcinoma, and cirrhosis complications.
The Paris International Liver Meeting convened more than 700 international hepatology specialists from 67 countries on January 19-21, 2026.

The authors characterize contemporary hepatology as shifting from end-stage complication management toward earlier detection, risk stratification, and disease modification using precision and mechanism-driven strategies.
The review reports that MASLD affects approximately 38% of the global population, representing more than 3 billion people.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: MASLD is one of the most prevalent chronic liver diseases globally, affecting approximately 38% of the world population

atoms.canonical_statement: The review reports that MASH affects 5%-7% of the general population.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: MASH, affects 5%-7% of the general population

atoms.canonical_statement: The narrative text reports that nearly 70% of people with type 2 diabetes have MASH/MASLD, while Figure 1 gives 65% for MASLD; the source is internally inconsistent on this estimate.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: Narrative: nearly 70%; Figure 1: 65% of patients with type 2 diabetes have MASLD

atoms.canonical_statement: In biopsy-characterized type 2 diabetes cohorts, the review reports advanced fibrosis (F3-F4) prevalence approaching 38%.
The review reports coronary heart disease prevalence of 44.6% in MASLD populations.
The authors frame MASLD/MASH as a systemic Cardiovascular-Kidney-Liver-Metabolic disorder requiring integrated care rather than a liver-only disease.
The review describes the guideline-recommended two-step MASLD algorithm as FIB-4 first, followed by VCTE for intermediate-risk patients.
The review cautions that FIB-4 is optimized to exclude advanced fibrosis in populations with low pre-test prevalence (<10%) and can yield more false negatives in enriched specialty cohorts.
Figure 2 uses FIB-4 >=1.3 as a threshold for progression to second-step testing with VCTE or ELF, while FIB-4 <1.3 is presented as low risk suitable for primary-care management.

The review proposes treatment-response monitoring using concordant non-invasive test changes rather than relying on a single marker, including a >=30% decrease in liver stiffness as one proposed response threshold.
The review reports a 22% increased MASLD risk associated with ultra-processed food exposure.
Figure 3 presents weight-loss targets of at least 5% to reduce liver fat, 7%-10% to improve liver inflammation, and at least 10% to improve fibrosis in patients with overweight/obesity.
The review reports that at least 150 minutes per week of moderate-to-vigorous exercise can produce clinically significant (>=30%) liver-fat reduction by imaging.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: At least 150min of moderate-to-vigorous weekly exercise ... induces clinically significant (>=30%) liver fat reduction measured by imaging

atoms.canonical_statement: The review reports that 10%-15% weight loss improves all histologic features of MASH, and bariatric surgery can induce MASH resolution in up to 85% within 1 year.

population.label: People with MASH undergoing bariatric surgery

atoms.canonical_statement: The review describes resmetirom as a selective thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonist approved for MASH with F2-F3 fibrosis; the reviewed trial dose highlighted is 80 mg orally once daily.
In the review's report of MAESTRO-NASH, resmetirom 80 mg achieved MASH resolution without fibrosis worsening in 25.9% versus 9.7% with placebo.

population.label: MAESTRO-NASH biopsy-proven MASH with F1-F3 fibrosis

atoms.canonical_statement: In the review's report of MAESTRO-NASH, fibrosis improvement of at least one stage occurred in 24.2% with resmetirom 80 mg versus 14.2% with placebo.

population.label: MAESTRO-NASH biopsy-proven MASH with F1-F3 fibrosis

atoms.canonical_statement: The review reports a mean LDL-cholesterol change of -13.6% with resmetirom 80 mg.
The review describes semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly as an approved GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy for MASH with F2-F3 fibrosis.
In the review's report of ESSENCE, semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly achieved MASH resolution without fibrosis worsening in 62.9% versus 34.3% with placebo.

population.label: ESSENCE biopsy-proven MASH with F2-F3 fibrosis

atoms.canonical_statement: In the review's report of ESSENCE, fibrosis improvement of at least one stage occurred in 36.8% with semaglutide versus 22.4% with placebo.

population.label: ESSENCE biopsy-proven MASH with F2-F3 fibrosis

atoms.canonical_statement: In ESSENCE as reported by the review, mean body-weight change was -10.5% with semaglutide versus -2.0% with placebo.

population.label: ESSENCE biopsy-proven MASH with F2-F3 fibrosis

atoms.canonical_statement: The review states that 55 agents are in phase 2-3 MASH development, illustrating the breadth of the therapeutic pipeline.
The review identifies FGF21 analogs as a class with phase 2b fibrosis-improvement signals including in compensated F4 cirrhosis, while emphasizing that confirmatory evidence is still needed.
The review reports randomized evidence that dapagliflozin can produce MASH resolution and fibrosis improvement, but does not provide the trial effect estimates in this review.
The review argues that combination therapy will likely be required to address heterogeneous MASH pathophysiology and the gap between MASH resolution and fibrosis improvement in advanced disease.

The review summarizes an EASL HBV treatment approach that treats HBsAg-positive patients with detectable HBV DNA when advanced fibrosis is present (LSM >8 kPa), or when HBV DNA >=2000 IU/mL is accompanied by elevated ALT, LSM >7 kPa, increased HCC risk, or transmission risk.

Figure 5 presents long-term nucleos(t)ide analogue monotherapy with tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, tenofovir alafenamide, or entecavir as first-line HBV therapy, with untreated patients monitored every 6-12 months.

The review states that end-of-treatment quantitative HBsAg <100 IU/mL in many studies is among the strongest predictors of safe nucleos(t)ide analogue discontinuation and sustained off-treatment response.
HBcrAg and HBV RNA are presented as complementary markers of residual HBV transcriptional activity that may refine decisions about treatment discontinuation.

Figure 6 recommends anti-HDV screening for all HBsAg-positive patients, reflex HDV RNA testing when anti-HDV is positive, fibrosis evaluation, HBV assessment, and consideration of bulevirtide with or without pegylated interferon.

The review reports that untreated chronic HDV has traditionally been associated with cirrhosis within 5-10 years and HCC within 15-20 years, while emphasizing substantial heterogeneity in progression.
The review describes bulevirtide as an NTCP entry inhibitor for chronic HDV, with the 2 mg once-daily dose authorized in Europe and prolonged therapy commonly required.

The review reports that 96 weeks of bulevirtide produced continuing combined virologic and biochemical responses at both 2 mg and 10 mg doses, with similar efficacy between doses and continued improvement among some week-24 suboptimal responders.
In the review's report of the phase 2 SOLSTICE trial, tobevibart plus elebsiran produced HBsAg <10 IU/mL in 91% of participants versus 21% with tobevibart monotherapy at week 48.
In the review's report of SOLSTICE, undetectable HDV RNA at week 48 occurred in 66% with tobevibart plus elebsiran versus 48% with tobevibart monotherapy.
The review describes PBC risk stratification as integrating age, biochemical response to UDCA, and liver stiffness; LSM >10 kPa identifies higher risk even when biochemical response is achieved.
The review lists POISE biochemical response as alkaline phosphatase <1.67 times ULN or at least 15% reduction together with normal bilirubin.

outcome.definition: ALP <1.67x ULN or >=15% reduction AND normal bilirubin

atoms.canonical_statement: The review reports robust phase 3 biochemical responses with elafibranor and seladelpar in PBC; seladelpar also met prespecified pruritus endpoints, whereas elafibranor did not meet its prespecified pruritus endpoint.
The review reports that contemporary 10-year transplant-free survival in PBC has improved to >85%-90% from approximately 70%-80% historically.
The review reports that fatigue affects 50%-80% of patients with PBC and remains a major unmet symptom need.
Figure 8 reports severe PBC pruritus quality-of-life score of 0.49, approaching severe Parkinson disease at 0.47; severe pruritus with severe depression is reported at 0.30.
The review identifies an implementation gap in PBC: fewer than 50% of eligible high-risk patients receive guideline-recommended second-line therapy.

The review characterizes PSC as lacking licensed disease-modifying therapy; approximately 70%-80% of patients have IBD and about two-thirds require liver transplantation or experience disease-related mortality within 20 years.
The review states that ursodeoxycholic acid in PSC can improve biochemical markers without demonstrated survival benefit and that high doses are harmful.
The review states that HCC surveillance for at-risk cirrhosis populations is ultrasound plus AFP every 6 months, with contrast-enhanced CT or MRI for nodules >1 cm.
Figure 10 reports standard ultrasound plus AFP surveillance sensitivity of 61% and specificity of 92%.

The review reports that immunotherapy-based combinations have shifted advanced HCC outcomes from historical median overall survival around 8 months toward approximately 24 months, with about 20% 5-year survival in selected contemporary populations.

The review reports TARE downstaging to UNOS T2 criteria in 58% versus 31% with TACE, while noting that these data come from phase 2 and retrospective evidence without phase 3 head-to-head confirmation.

concept.text: Successful downstaging to UNOS T2 criteria

atoms.canonical_statement: In the review's report of IMbrave150, atezolizumab plus bevacizumab achieved median overall survival of 19.2 months versus 13.2 months with sorafenib.
The review reports exploratory post hoc 5-year overall survival of 20% with the STRIDE regimen.
The review reports a 36% response rate with first-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab, while noting a notable hepatotoxicity profile.

The review notes that recent phase 3 triple-combination immunotherapy trials have not improved on doublet efficacy, suggesting a therapeutic plateau and increasing the importance of biomarker-guided selection.

The Baveno VII CSPH rule-in threshold summarized by the review is LSM >25 kPa; the rule-out combination LSM <15 kPa plus platelet count >=150 G/L is reported to have 99% negative predictive value across etiologies.
The review reports that adding spleen stiffness to refined Baveno VII criteria can reduce the indeterminate CSPH zone from 48% to as low as 9%.

concept.text: Refined Baveno VII criteria with spleen stiffness

atoms.canonical_statement: The review treats recompensated cirrhosis after etiologic cure as a distinct disease stage with better prognosis than decompensated cirrhosis and as a meaningful clinical-trial endpoint.
For salvage TIPS, the review reports >85% 6-week survival when lactate <=2.5 mmol/L and MELD <=15, versus >90% mortality when lactate >=12 mmol/L and/or MELD >=30.

population.label: Patients receiving salvage TIPS for refractory variceal bleeding

atoms.canonical_statement: The review reports that preemptive TIPS in the GAVAPROSEC randomized trial reduced rebleeding or death at 1 year for acute non-GOV1 gastric variceal bleeding and argues for broader first-line use in fundal variceal bleeding.

The review summarizes revised HRS-AKI guidance as no longer requiring routine 48-hour albumin administration for diagnosis; when volume depletion is suspected, response to individualized fluid resuscitation should be assessed within 24 hours.

A study summarized by the review found that 34% of patients with cirrhosis and AKI showed albumin responsiveness between 24 and 48 hours, raising concern that a 24-hour diagnostic window can miss delayed responders.

population.label: Patients with cirrhosis and acute kidney injury

atoms.canonical_statement: The review reports 1-year mortality of 64% after hepatic encephalopathy onset versus 17% in patients without decompensation.

The review states that ammonia measurement should complement rather than replace clinical assessment for hepatic encephalopathy; a normal ammonia level should prompt diagnostic reconsideration, while elevation alone does not reliably grade severity.
The review identifies lactulose as first-line therapy for hepatic encephalopathy and rifaximin added to lactulose as effective for reducing recurrent episodes and HE-related hospitalizations.

For recurrent or refractory HE associated with large spontaneous portosystemic shunts, the review states that shunt embolization can reduce recurrence in selected patients but may worsen portal hypertension.

The authors identify real-world implementation barriers to MASH therapy including GLP-1 receptor agonist discontinuation from gastrointestinal adverse effects, variable adherence, and heterogeneous treatment response.

The authors identify major research needs including long-term MASH safety and durability over 5-10 years, mechanisms of heterogeneous treatment response, and evidence for underrepresented populations including pregnant, pediatric, and non-obese patients.
The work was supported by The Global NASH/MASH Council and the Association Pour le Developpment de La Recherche sur les Maladies du Foie (ADRMF).
The manuscript contains extensive author-level financial disclosures involving multiple pharmaceutical, biotechnology, diagnostics, and medical-device companies.
The authors state that data supporting the findings are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.
